pathophysiology.summary: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk is the combined effect of age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, lipids, diabetes, kidney disease and family history. Estimating 10-year risk targets preventive treatment to those most likely to benefit.
keyMechanisms: Atherogenic lipoproteins, hypertension, smoking and hyperglycaemia damage the endothelium and drive plaque formation.
Risk factors multiply rather than add — hence multivariable risk tools.
Statins lower LDL and reduce events in proportion to baseline risk.

symptoms: Usually asymptomatic; ask about smoking, family history of premature CVD, diabetes, kidney disease.
physicalSigns: BP, BMI and waist circumference; xanthomas (familial hypercholesterolaemia).
redFlags: BP 180/120 or above with symptoms — urgent
Total cholesterol above 9.0 or non-HDL above 7.5 mmol/L — specialist (NICE)
Chest pain or claudication — investigate as established disease

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Secondary prevention pathway — not risk scoring.
Very high LDL, family history — FH pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Record smoking, BP, BMI/waist, lipids, glucose and family history (PHA checklist).
Estimate 10-year CVD risk; do not score people with established CVD, type 1 diabetes, CKD or FH — treat as high risk (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Lifestyle
actions: Stop smoking; diet; physical activity; weight management (PHA checklist; NICE NG238 1.6.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Statin
actions: PHA (USPSTF-based): statin for adults 40–75 with 1 or more risk factor and 10-year risk 10% or more; selectively for 7.5–10%.
NICE: atorvastatin 20 mg if QRISK3 10% or more after lifestyle discussion.

clinicalManagement.title: Aspirin
actions: Aspirin 81 mg daily for primary prevention at 40–59 with 10-year risk 10% or more is an individual decision — net benefit small; best if low bleeding risk (PHA).
